```{r, setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# load tidyverse package which includes dplyr and ggplot - the two packages we will need
library(tidyverse)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)

```

## 1) Download the Sample RNA-seq Count Matrix and associated Metadata.

```{r}

# Read in both data sets
count.df <- read.csv(file = "data/counts.csv", header = TRUE)
meta_data.df <- read.csv(file = "data/meta_data.csv", header = TRUE)
```

### Data wrangling over the next sequence of steps

```{r, message=FALSE}
# Use only 5 columns of data in the meta_data dataframe to make processing faster
metadata.modified <- meta_data.df %>%
  dplyr::select(1,10,23,29,41,86) %>%
  # The barcode variable will eventually be used to join the metadata to the count data
  # The hyphen in the barcode variable needs to be changed to a dot
  mutate(barcode = str_replace_all(barcode, "-", "."))

```

```{r, message=FALSE}

# Convert count.df to long format
# This is required for many of the ggplot graphs and many other functions in R
# Use the pivot_longer function to convert the count dataframe to one I am calling
# dat.long which will end up containing three columns - the Ensembl ID, one called
# Samples which will contain all of the individual sample values and one called
# Counts which will contain the gene_expression count values

dat.long <- count.df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -X,        # Pivot all columns except the one containing the Ensemble ID
    names_to = "Samples",    # Column name for your old wide headers
    values_to = "Counts"    # Column name for your data values
  )

```


```{r, message=FALSE}
# This code block is where I join the dat.long dataframe for the counts to the 
# metadata dataframe for the additional information needed for the assignment
# The results of the join are stored in a new dataframe.
# dat.long$Samples is joined on metadata.modified$barcode
dat.long.enriched <- dat.long %>%
  mutate(X = sub("\\.[^.]*$", "", X)) %>% # Strip off version number
  inner_join(., metadata.modified, by = c("Samples" = "barcode"))

```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# This code block is used to map the Ensembl IDs to their actual gene symbol.

# Load required libraries
library(AnnotationDbi) # provides an R interface to query SQLite-based biological 
                       # annotation database
library(org.Hs.eg.db)  # Used to access genome-wide human annotations based primarily on 
                       # Entrez Gene identifiers

# The Ensemble ID has a "version" number on it that needs to be stripped off because
# the gene_symbols generated do not have it.
count.df.mod <- count.df %>%
  mutate(X = sub("\\.[^.]*$", "", X))

# Now need to pull the processed Ensemble ID's out into a vector
ensembl.ids <- count.df.mod %>% pull(X)

# This is the heart of the process where the Ensemble ID is mapped to Gene Symbols
# Uses he mapIds() function from AnnotationDbi. Maps identifiers for genomic data by 
# connecting a set of input keys to target columns using annotation databases
gene_symbols <- mapIds(
  x = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keys = ensembl.ids,
  keytype = "ENSEMBL",
  column = "SYMBOL",
  multiVals = "first" # Keeps the first match if duplicate mappings occur
)

# Store the results in a dataframe "df" for use in a following join operation
df <- data.frame(names(gene_symbols),gene_symbols)

```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# This is where I merge the previously created dataframe "df" that contains the
# actual mapping from Ensembl ID to gene using an inner join
dat.long.genes <- dat.long.enriched %>%
  inner_join(., df, by = c("X" = "names.gene_symbols."))

```

All of the data wrangling has been completed up to this point. Additional steps
will be required when we create the heat map

## 2) Gene selection and Summary Statistics

```{r, Q2}

# I am choosing the gene BRCA1 to study
# BRCA1 is a human tumor suppressor genes that normally produce proteins to repair damaged 
# DNA and prevent uncontrolled cell growth

get_mode <- function(x) {
  uniq_x <- unique(x)
  uniq_x[which.max(tabulate(match(x, uniq_x)))]
}

# Using dplyr filter out only BRCA1 and do summary statistics
summary_stats <- dat.long.genes %>%
  filter(gene_symbols == 'BRCA1') %>%
  summarize(
    min = min(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
    mode = get_mode(Counts),
    sd = sd(Counts, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
summary_stats
  

```

## 3) Visualization

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=6, out.width="100%}
# a) Create a Histogram: Use ggplot2 to generate a histogram of the count data for the selected gene.
# This visualization should effectively display the distribution of the counts.

# Using dplyr, filter for the BRCA1 gene and use the ajcc_pathologic_stage as fill aesthetic.
# The ajcc_pathologic_stage is a standardized cancer classification assigned after a 
# patient undergoes surgical resection of the primary tumor.
# Generate a histogram using geom_histogram from ggplot2()

png("images/Distribution of BRCA1 Counts.png",
        width = 800, height = 600, res = 100)

dat.long.genes %>%
  filter(gene_symbols == 'BRCA1') %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=Counts)) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.5, 
                   fill = "blue", 
                   binwidth = 100,
                   na.rm = TRUE) +
     labs(
        title = "Distribution of BRCA1 Counts",
        x = "BRCA1 RNA-Sequencing Counts",
        y = "Count of Samples"
     ) +
     theme_minimal() + 
     theme(
       plot.title = element_text(
         face = "bold",
         hjust = 0.5
       )
     )  

dev.off()
```
\newpage

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, out.width="90%}
# b) Create a Scatter Plot: Select a second gene from the dataset. Create a scatter plot using 
# ggplot2 to compare the count data of the two selected genes.

# make a vector of the genes of interest - BRCA2 is also a human tumor suppressor gene
genes.of.interest <- c('BRCA1', 'BRCA2')

# Using dplyr, filter for the genes of interest. Then, using the select verb, select all columns
# except column 1 prior to pivoting back from the current long form of data to the wide form
# This is required for the scatter plot.
# Use the sample_type as the factor variable in the plot

png("images/BRCA1 vs BRCA2 RNA-seq Counts.png",
        width = 800, height = 600, res = 100)

dat.long.genes %>%
  filter(gene_symbols %in% genes.of.interest) %>%
  dplyr::select(-1) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = gene_symbols, values_from = Counts) %>%
  filter(!is.na(paper_BRCA_Subtype_PAM50)) %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x = BRCA1,y = BRCA2)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = factor(paper_BRCA_Subtype_PAM50)),
             alpha = 0.5, 
             size = 2, 
             na.rm = TRUE) +
             scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
             scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
             scale_color_discrete(name = "Factor Values") +  #Legend title
             annotation_logticks(sides = "bl") + 
             labs(title = "BRCA1 vs BRCA2 RNA-seq Counts",
                subtitle = "Counts given in logarithmetic scales",
                x = "BRCA1 RNA-sequencing Counts",
                y = "BRCA2 RNA-sequencing Counts"
             ) +
             theme(
                 plot.title = element_text(
                 face = "bold",
                 hjust = 0.5
            ),
                 plot.subtitle = element_text(
                 hjust = 0.5
            ) 
  )
dev.off()
```

```{r, DataLoad, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
count.df <- read.csv(file = "data/counts.csv", header = TRUE,row.names = 1)
meta_data.df <- read.csv(file = "data/meta_data.csv", header = TRUE)
```

```{r, DataWrangling, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Recommended 10-gene core BRCA/HR variant panel For mutation/variant analysis
genes.of.interest <- c("ENSG00000012048.23","ENSG00000139618.16",
                       "ENSG00000083093.10","ENSG00000138376.11",
                       "ENSG00000108384.15", "ENSG00000185379.20",
                       "ENSG00000136492.9", "ENSG00000149311.19",
                       "ENSG00000183765.23", "ENSG00000167258.15")

gene_name <- c("BRCA1", "BRCA2", "PALB2", "BARD1", "RAD51C",
                "RAD51D", "BRIP1", "ATM", "CHEK2", "CDK12")

count.df.subset <- count.df %>%
  filter(rownames(.) %in% genes.of.interest)

count.df.matrix <- as.matrix(count.df.subset[,])

# Rename from Ensebml ID to Gene
rownames(count.df.matrix) <- gene_name

rownames(count.df.subset) <- gene_name

```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(conflicted)
conflict_prefer("select", "dplyr")

count.df.subset %>% 
  mutate(row_mean = rowMeans(select(., where(is.numeric)), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  select(last_col())
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
count.df.subset.long <- count.df.subset %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Gene") %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Gene, 
    names_to = "Sample", 
    values_to = "Counts"
  )
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Define your target strings
targets <- c("Adjuvant", "Anastrozole", "First-Line Therapy", "Carboplatin","Paclitaxel")
pattern <- paste(targets, collapse = "|")

# Extract the matching string into a new column
meta_data.df.corrected_2 <- meta_data.df %>% 
  mutate(treatment_method = str_extract(treatments, pattern))
```


```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
meta_data.df.corrected_2 <- meta_data.df.corrected_2 %>% mutate(barcode = str_replace_all(barcode, "-", "."))

meta_data.df.corrected_2 %>% arrange(treatment_method)
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
count.df.subset.enriched <- count.df.subset.long %>%
  inner_join(., meta_data.df.corrected_2, by = c("Sample" = "barcode"))
```

```{r}
df3 <- count.df.subset.enriched %>%
  group_by(sample_type, Gene, treatment_method) %>%
  summarise(mean_value = mean(Counts, na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r, size="tiny"}

conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr")

# Generate additional covariate statistics
covariate_summary_statistics <- count.df.subset.enriched %>%
  filter(Gene == "ATM") %>%
  filter(!is.na(treatment_method)) %>%
  filter(Counts <= 25000) %>%
  group_by(treatment_method) %>%
  summarise(mean_value = mean(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean = mean(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
            mode = get_mode(Counts),
            std = sd(Counts, na.rm = TRUE))

covariate_summary_statistics_data <- count.df.subset.enriched %>%
  filter(Gene == "ATM") %>%
  filter(Counts <= 25000) %>%
  filter(!is.na(treatment_method)) %>%
  group_by(treatment_method)

model1 <- lm(Counts ~ treatment_method, covariate_summary_statistics_data)
cat("\n")
cat("ATM Gene Covariate Summary Statistics.\n")
cat("\n")
print(covariate_summary_statistics)
cat("\n")
cat("LM Model Summary.\n")
summary(model1)
cat("\n")
cat("Anova Summary.\n")
anova_model <- aov(model1)
summary(anova_model)
cat("\n")
cat("Tukey HSD Results.\n")
cat("\n")
tukey_results <- TukeyHSD(anova_model)
print(tukey_results)

```


```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, out.width="90%}

png("images/Distribution of BRCA1 Gene Counts by Treatment Method.png",
        width = 800, height = 600, res = 100)

df3 %>%
  filter(!is.na(treatment_method)) %>%
  filter(mean_value <= 25000) %>%
ggplot(., aes(x = treatment_method, y = mean_value, fill = Gene)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 22000)) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution Gene Counts by Treatment Method",
    x = "Treatment Method",
    y = "Counts",
    fill = "Stage"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(vjust = 0.5))

dev.off()
```

### New Heatmap

```{r}
heatmap_colors <- colorRamp2(
  c(-2,0,2),
  c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B")
)

```


```{r}
# Define color schemes for all annotations
colour_list <- list(
  laterality <- c("Left" = "blue", "Right" = "orange")
  #sample_type = col2rgb(unname(c("Primary Tumor" = "red", "Solid Tissue Normal" = "green"))),
  #treatment_method = col2rgb(unname(c("Adjuvant" = "white", "Anastrozole" = "red",
  #                     "Carboplatin" = "green", "First-Line Therapy" = "blue")))
)
```

```{r}
# Create top annotation for continuous variables
top_ann <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Laterality = meta_data.df.corrected_2$laterality,
  Sample_type = meta_data.df.corrected_2$sample_type,
  
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  annotation_legend_param = list(
    Laterality = list(title = "Laterality"),
    Sample_type = list(title = "Sample Type")
  )
  #colour_list = list(laterality = Laterality)
)

# Create bottom annotation for treatment variables
bottom_ann <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Treatment_Method = meta_data.df.corrected_2$treatment_method,

  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10)
 
)
```

```{r}
# Heatmap with annotations
annotated_heatmap <- Heatmap(
  count.df.matrix,
  name = "Expression",
  
  #col = colour_list,
  # Clustering parameters
  clustering_distance_rows = "spearman",
  clustering_method_rows = "ward.D2",
  clustering_distance_columns = "spearman",
  clustering_method_columns = "ward.D2",
  column_split = meta_data.df.corrected_2$treatment_method,
  
  top_annotation = top_ann,
  bottom_annotation = bottom_ann,
  
  
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  row_names_side = "left",
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  
  column_title = "Gene Expression"
)

png("images/Gene Expression Heatmap.png",
        width = 800, height = 600, res = 100)
draw(annotated_heatmap)
dev.off()
```
